## Status vocabulary

- **T**: reviewed implementation plus named targeted test evidence. This is not
  exhaustive proof for all inputs, platforms or failure interleavings.
- **C**: code reviewed, but targeted evidence for the full clause remains incomplete.
- **P**: partial implementation/evidence; the stated gap remains open.
- **O**: not yet resolved by this clause audit; do not infer conformance from E2E success.
- **S**: obligation of the Sendspin server, not of this client SDK. Receiver-side
  shape/lifecycle checks are recorded separately where relevant.
- **D**: optional feature or recommendation deliberately not implemented, with rationale.

Normative field descriptions and non-keyword sequencing rules also matter.
Counting uppercase MUST/SHOULD occurrences alone is not a complete audit.

## Atomic normative review

The legacy groups below retain their IDs and assessments. The following
obligations are independently classified, not inherited test verdicts. `complete`
means a group's classification was reviewed, not that its obligations are met.
`must-not`/`should-not` preserve polarity; `basis` distinguishes explicit keywords,
declarative protocol contracts and nonbinding examples. An unselected `may` can
disable a conditional branch only through an explicit `enabled_by` link; it cannot
erase unrelated client MUSTs or recommendations.

Software and hardware evidence remain different. Each obligation lists its own
tests, assessment and remaining work; passing tests never fill missing measurement
or normative decisions. The execution report adds a prioritized, still-partial
backlog and lists all groups without completed atomic classification. All **148
historical groups have now received atomic review**. This does not mean that
every classification question has been resolved: **145 are completely classified,
three remain partial**, with their unresolved atoms and reasons intact.

The pass covers the core, connection/discovery, player, controller, metadata,
color, artwork, visualizer and pairing groups in the nine pinned documents.
Shared format/header/capacity/state predicates retain canonical IDs across groups.
P08, CN15 and MD01 retain explicit classification questions. The separate
[review-decision ledger](rc1-review-decisions.md) resolves five other group
classifications without certifying their security, integration or printed-QR
evidence. No untouched historical group is hidden in that list.
Codec-header lexical validation found during this review has real regression and
encrypted-reference evidence; the review is not merely a reassignment of labels.
Specifically, Go's standard Base64 decoder ignored CR/LF and custom factories
previously bypassed that lexical check. Regressions reproduced both cases; the
core dispatch and public FLAC decoder now enforce canonical standard Base64.
Replacement decoders still own codec contents, not a license to weaken known
wire syntax. Additional representation/ordering/restart assertions remain explicit
proof gaps rather than automatically inheriting the old grouped `T` assessments.

Unpaired-access/token/code-profile decisions now also distinguish local SDK policy,
operator parser contract, remote approval/UI and physical product printing. The
actual hello policy boolean and rejection of inverse remote-policy fields have
independent encrypted-peer tests; the emitter has a fixed independent reference
separate from decoder roundtrips. No live policy-toggle or code-method feature is
introduced. R13's live withdrawal and R15's printed-label duties are now classified
as conditional SDK/product contracts; their evidence remains incomplete rather
than disappearing into optional or server-only labels. The finer
code-flow state/field and server verification decomposition is now recorded;
it is not implementation evidence for either unoffered code method.

The controller/metadata/color pass now shares state replacement, omission and
role-removal predicates rather than duplicating them for each role. Server group
redistribution/cycles and WCAG palette constraints are not client implementation
tasks. A receiver unit explicitly preserves opaque metadata and component-valid
RGB values without inventing URL/year ranges or a palette-generation engine.
MD01.06 leaves the current decoder's negative numeric-field rejection unresolved:
tests of that policy and a helper oracle with the same assumptions cannot prove
that the pinned integer field definitions require it. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

Artwork now separates declaration, exact transfer grammar, cross-channel in-flight
state, scheduling and clear/end behavior from server scaling, padding, pacing and
late-join duties. Visualizer separates request/echo grammar, per-frame layouts,
ordering, stale/unavailable discard and local byte accounting from server analysis
quality, periodic rates and the server-clock capacity ledger. Generic core rules
do not acquire passing evidence merely because a role's narrow test passed.
The targeted software-evidence pass now independently checks literal fragment
bytes/size transitions, all supported-role hello subsets, all active-role state
subsets, role reactivation and explicit/omitted clear/end targets. Exact expected
wire values do not come from the SDK's own decoder or a symmetric roundtrip.
It reproduced two stream/end errors: a shared clear/end Go model imposed typing
on an unknown end field, and an uncancelled artwork transfer could be detected
only after another target had already ended. Both have direct regressions and
were fixed without relaxing clear's known timestamp checks.

An encrypted scripted peer also carries current/pending presentation states,
complete/in-flight artwork and decoded visualization through same-version
activations and two actual rekeys in both suites. Direct actor dispatch and a
controlled test clock establish software retention/order, not independent crypto,
aiosendspin/native-platform behavior, elapsed-time scheduling or physical display
timing. Native discovery and physical measurements remain separate work.

The remaining software-evidence pass now gives every previously open software
entry its own targeted assertions: receive-time codec changes, distinct PCM
channels/Opus packet framing, unavailable audio, send-ahead invariance, actual
replay/out-of-order closure and fragment checks, role-independent core handling,
FileStore nondefault restarts, credential generation provenance, new-key trust
categories and pairing cancellation/contention. Exact outgoing field inventories
and the full reason vocabulary are guarded separately from peer acceptance.
An actual actor-timer trace adds elapsed-budget evidence alongside cooperative
Store tests; it is not hard-real-time preemption of arbitrary callbacks/native I/O.

The outbound pairing-only reconnect gap was reproduced and fixed: final declared
purpose now survives transport cleanup, so Run ends that attempt instead of
silently replaying it. Handshake/idle/playback retries, explicit reason handling
and capped/reset backoff have independent checks. No normative classification,
physical measurement or unsupported code-method feature is promoted by these
software results. Three group classifications remain partial after the separate
source-based review, not as a consequence of passing tests.

The [working-assumption ledger](rc1-working-assumptions.md) now pins a separate
`sendspin-cpp` implementation comparison. Its provisional decisions permit targeted
software work without test results resolving normative classification. The
generated policy section records differences and revisit conditions; policy test
results never become normative or physical evidence by inheritance. Separately
fingerprinted template.md context distinguishes R:19's uppercase SHOULD from its
lowercase QR suggestion, without claiming the whole template is atomically
inventoried. The strict gate retains mandatory security/withdrawal/printed-label
blockers even though those groups are now classified.

### Informational language-tag policy

The SDK checks ASCII RFC 5646 section 2.1 structure (including all grandfathered
forms) and the duplicate variant/singleton restrictions from section 2.2.9.
The production scanner is checked against fixed RFC examples and a separately
written test-only ABNF regular expression in `FuzzLanguageTag`. This is **not**
IANA registry validation or extension-specific semantic validation. Unknown,
structurally sound subtags remain usable hints instead of being rejected by an
outdated registry snapshot. Locale identifiers such as `de_DE`, language ranges
such as `*`, malformed tags, nulls and empty language lists are not valid wire hints.

No tag is canonicalized, matched, reordered or silently repaired. Applications
can use `Snapshot.ServerLanguages` to choose their own operator-facing output;
this PSK-only SDK does not implement spoken/displayed pairing-code output or its
RFC 4647 language lookup. The server name and language hint are connection-wide,
not role state, and survive role changes/key re-handshakes. A second server/hello
is a sequencing violation, not a hint update. These are still peer-provided data,
not proof of peer authentication when unpaired access is enabled.

The source support **outer object** is a known core field. Its role-specific
contents are neither validated nor retained: core message obligations do not
require an implementation of a role this client never advertises. Unknown future
support-object keys are ignored without inspecting their values. This is not
evidence that an injected partial source capability is a conformant server offer.

### Connection and timeout evidence boundaries

Native reference tests leave the independent Noise/pairing/index/compliance checks
enabled. For the delayed-first-write timeout, the SDK's test observer changes only
its actor-owned deadline at the completed-transmission boundary; it does not log
the redacted pairing body or change the peer's state machine. The test proves no
client/finalize disclosure after expiry, one timeout abort and a working native
retry with the next pairing index.

The late-finalize case manually drives the production dispatcher over a real
encrypted native reference connection **without starting the actor ticker**. It
receives the peer's actual post-persistence finalize and expires the local attempt
before processing it. The confirmation cannot win merely because its receive case
was selected before a timer. A peer that already committed can retain that record;
local expiry is not a distributed rollback protocol.

Timeout is checked at local acceptance, including after a blocked send and before
a credential transaction after mutex acquisition. Unit tests cover the exact
inclusive boundary, idempotent cleanup, stale-message discard and preservation of
unrelated roles/streams/group state. Re-handshake's no-application-write gate is
not bypassed: the next activation supersedes the old attempt. These finite checks
do not certify a two-minute wall-clock bound under arbitrary blocking Store I/O,
user callbacks, scheduling stalls or native-driver calls.

The common-pairing atomic pass found that local persistence previously received
only the session context. Even a context-cooperative Save could therefore wait
past the attempt deadline. It now receives a child context with that deadline.
Unit tests preserve independent earlier Store/parent errors; a native peer test
manually drives the dispatcher, receives a real post-persistence finalize, then
lets a cooperative local Save expire **without an actor ticker**. The local pending
key/protection are cleared and an actual timeout abort is observed, while the
peer's committed record remains. This is not a claim of rollback, interruptible
mutex/native calls or an unconditional physical wall-clock bound.

### Handshake matrix and its independence boundary

`client_handshake_test.go` runs a scripted Go peer in both WebSocket directions
with both RC1 cipher suites. It implements its own JSON framing, Noise sequence,
fragment headers and failure transcript checks, without SDK `Channel`, parsing or
fragment helpers on the peer side. It **shares the upstream Noise primitive** and
therefore complements, but does not replace, the independent aiosendspin tests or
constitute an independent cryptographic implementation.

The matrix covers malformed initial/inner/rekey fields, wrong UTF-8/Base64/category,
tamper, wrong prologue/suite and rekey lookup miss; premature applications before
hello/activation or under old keys after rekey; and stalled init, Noise message 1,
initial activation or new-key activation. Each script requires connection closure
without further data messages, unchanged credentials/history and released session
reservations. Valid old-key clock requests may cross before rekey message 2.
WebSocket control-close frames are not application data responses. Server/error
cases establish safe refusal, not authenticated reasons or reason-specific retry
and diagnostic classification.

Positive controls independently verify the literal `{}` message-2 payload, raw
prologue bytes with unknown fields/whitespace and resumed clock exchange after
new-key activation. A separate boundary test accepts exactly 65535 raw Noise bytes
in the initial JSON/base64 carrier and an independently fragmented rekey, then
rejects a valid-AEAD 65536-byte transport packet. Initial text input is bounded to
128 KiB; the WebSocket transport cap returns to 65535 bytes after key installation.
This is not an exhaustive write-failure, cancellation, socket-load or RFC 6455
frame-boundary matrix, nor a hardware/runtime-platform certification.

### Write-failure and cancellation evidence

`client_handshake_write_test.go` covers 152 I/O scenarios across both cipher
suites: 76 outbound post-upgrade Client-handler cases and 76 inbound cases through
the actual `ServeHTTP` path. Only underlying `net.Conn` instances are wrapped; SDK
framing, Noise and actor logic remain unchanged. Six targets cover client/init, initial/rekey message 2,
hello and initial/new-key role-state writes. Each has zero-byte, prefix, complete
carrier-then-error, cancellation and successful-control variants. Separate cases
exercise local handshake write deadlines and a failed continuation of a three-part
client hello.

The incoming listener wraps the accepted socket before net/http sees it. Its
HTTP 101 response is passed through unchanged, and client/init fault injection is
armed only once the header has actually been sent. The test verifies the inbound
mode reservation at the target write and its release after `ServeHTTP` returns.
Successful-carrier fault cases inspect the actual mask bit: SDK writes are masked
outbound and unmasked inbound. Neither direction is inferred merely from a label.

The injected connection honors Close and changing write deadlines. An independently
tested RFC 6455 tracker distinguishes net.Conn writes, masked/extended frame
headers, continuation frames and complete WebSocket messages. The peer confirms
that a complete message 2 can arrive even when the local Write reports failure;
the SDK then closes without later data, retains the old category/record binding
for the failed rekey and releases the session. The fragment test confirms no final
part or successful logical-send observation after the failed continuation. Controls
at each target complete normally; partial prefixes are not misclassified as full
carrier delivery.

These tests use idle/role activations with no playback activity, so no history or
credential writes are expected. They do not roll back legitimate earlier saves,
undo remote receipt of message 2, certify storage failures, or model actual kernel
backpressure, native OS socket behavior and every cancellation interleaving. The
peer still shares the Noise primitive. Passing cases required no SDK change in
outbound and inbound audit passes; evidence remains separate from normative fulfillment.

### Admission and record-capacity boundaries

Initial admission publishes the new holder and its declared rank under the same
mutex; another contender must not observe the default idle rank in between.
Cancellation is checked after waiting for the admission mutex, before deciding
displacement, and before final publication. This does not undo a handoff already
decided before a later cancellation or guarantee interruptible mutex/native waits.

`TestReferenceConcurrentInadmissibleActivationsCannotEnterAdmission` holds that
admission mutex while three real encrypted peer connections deliver malformed,
unauthorized and pairing-required activations. The valid holder still processes a
same-direction barrier, with no new credential writes or pairing disclosure.
These activations are explicit fault injections; peer Noise and ordinary writer
behavior remain unchanged. This is not every malformed-message/interleaving matrix.

The full-store peer test uses five records and four open sessions. It gates three
actual outgoing long-term Noise responses before `Handshake` returns a Channel;
the fourth native pairing persists exactly one new record without evicting the
three protected ones. Selection protects a new long-term record immediately, but
a later pr/sn rekey releases an old record only after transport-key commit. Unit
tests separately cover that pending-rekey/commit eviction boundary. Early socket
capacity rejection remains pre-authentication and carries no encrypted priority
reason; broader authenticated resource-refusal/load behavior remains open.

### Buffered playback and device-transition evidence

`client_playback_lifecycle_e2e_test.go` injects explicit valid PCM stream messages
through the independent reference's real encrypted writer. Its ordinary role
controls and native PSK pairing protocol remain enabled. A virtual output gates
one write while a second decoded chunk is queued. Clear/end/removal cancel that
write and flush before fresh data; a Sentinel-to-pairing-to-long-term promotion
instead preserves both old-key chunks, their order and the existing device/stream.
The virtual output clock deliberately pauses at the gate: these tests establish
ownership and buffer lifecycle, not elapsed-time scheduling or physical stop time.
They do not certify all remote server stream-generation policies.

Worker-level barriers separately cover reset during a pending Open, blocked Write
or format-drain Next, failed flush, terminal drain/close errors and an independent
backend `context.Canceled` while the work context is still live. A canceled drain
does not open its obsolete format; a failed Close is not retried during cleanup.
Arbitrary blocking native calls, driver cleanup guarantees and gapless physical
rate/channel switching remain outside these finite software checks.

### Control test boundaries

Native controller capability setters, role transitions and player-state readers in
the reference server provide the positive scenarios. Explicit malformed peer states
and remote player commands use the existing encrypted fault writer. They are not
evidence the reference normally emits invalid values. Optional fixture observations
retain only known numeric/boolean control fields and command identifiers, never
credentials or audio. They record the actual decrypted client message before native
dispatch; controller backend effects remain server/application responsibilities.

The unsupported-player-command exception applies only after a valid player object
and string command discriminator, on an active role and after core activation.
It does not waive JSON/UTF-8 validation, role checks, or argument checks for any
offered command. Controller state is still a complete typed snapshot, even when
its command list is empty or only relative seek is available.

### In-flight artwork evidence

`ArtworkWireProbe` in `internal/e2e/media.py` pauses the encrypted writer **after**
a first native multipart part was transmitted. A valid group marker follows that
part in the same direction, before the pause; the Go test sees it before asserting
that the current image is still complete and unchanged. Replacement/cancel/removal
then use native reference role APIs, not a substitute cancellation implementation.
Header/count traces prove ordering, and encoded source hashes check the complete
late replacement. Generated PNGs are bounded; the pause is a synchronization
fixture, not a playback/load measurement. Other malformed-message cases are raw
peer faults, not a claim about normal reference behavior.

`FuzzRoleBinaryMessages` checks retained/discarded byte counts, pending/partial
exclusion and per-image/visualizer limits with cancellation seeds. The remaining
resource, clock-domain and rendering audits are not closed by these finite tests.

the SDK nor its tests substitute a waveform-analysis implementation for the server.

### Pairing test boundaries

`internal/e2e/pairing_observer.py` optionally observes decrypted transport message
names plus bounded numeric indices/defined abort reasons. It never stores PSKs,
Noise data or complete pairing bodies. Its explicit fault mode replaces a native
activation on the real encrypted writer, or inserts stale messages just before
the native cancelling activation. This is **fault injection**, not a claim that
the reference normally emits those messages. The native server still owns the
attempt, checks the client's response/index, persists, re-handshakes and recovers.
Its strict compliance guards are not disabled or monkey-patched.

The concurrent handoff case uses bounded send/receive observation barriers during a
real re-handshake, and gates any native follow-up activation at the reference writer.
It proves the already-decided displacement completes with the required goodbye
even when the old server does not send another activation after the refusal.

A raw activation that invents a pairing attempt without telling the reference's
state machine is unsuitable for refusal/recovery tests: it causes the strict peer
to reject the client's correct abort as unsolicited. Those cases therefore use
native PSK attempts with controlled outgoing field faults instead. Pure schema
failures can still be injected directly because they require no response.

The nine-document paragraph reference/context pass is accounted for in the
machine catalog; this does not complete the atomic normative inventory or close
the partial implementation/evidence statuses below. Context/example dispositions
are visible separately from requirement and execution results in the report.

1. Continue the field-by-field known-message validation/direction matrix beyond
   hello/activation, including conditional/ignored fields and malformed values
   while unavailable. M13's informational-tag policy is not a general locale engine.
2. Extend the connection/PSK C rows: native handshake write/cancellation/load
   cases beyond the finite malformed-phase/timeout and bidirectional I/O matrices, broader
   concurrent inadmissible admissions, resource-cap refusal paths, broader buffered-media rekey and
   blocking-I/O timeout behavior. Code-pairing methods and source audio remain
   unadvertised; token input is now covered separately from strict wire encoding.
3. Extend the remaining C/S media resource, late-join and concurrent-load evidence
   where it applies to this SDK, without turning receiver interoperability into
   a blanket certification of server analysis or physical rendering.
4. Extend the new predicted-output sliding-window and timestamp-boundary tests
   with resource pressure and cancellation/load interleavings, then measure
   physical audio output, actual speed and correction audibility. The numerical
   budget does not establish rare one-shot recovery or hardware conformance.

## Provisional working assumptions (not normative evidence)

Pinned C++ source inspection informs these policies; it is not a C++ runtime test or a conformance proof. Passing policy tests do not resolve the linked normative obligations.

### WA01 — provisional

Linked obligations: P08.04, P08.05, P08.06, P08.07, P08.08, P08.09, P08.10. Policy evidence: **declared, not executed here**.

Decision: Keep application-configured immutable startup/minimum-buffer hints for this SDK profile. Do not require an automatic arrival-delay estimator before continuing targeted software work; do not add output delay to either hint.

Reason / differences: The pinned C++ config reports a configured or pipeline-derived startup lead, explicitly not a measured one, and a configured min_buffer_ms (default 500). Its player state uses these values. This supports a practical static-profile assumption, not normative permission to ignore estimator recommendations or a reason to copy its 500-ms default into Go. Go values remain deployment inputs, not measured optimums.

Revisit when: Authoritative clarification of P:65, adding runtime estimation, a changed output pipeline, or deployment underrun/startup measurements. Physical latency and convergence remain separate obligations.

### WA02 — provisional

Linked obligations: MD01.05, MD01.06, MD01.07, MD01.08. Policy evidence: **declared, not executed here**.

Decision: Support nonnegative int64 progress/duration/per-thousand-speed fields, including zero duration and paused speed zero. Retain rejection of negative fields, complete required progress grammar and silent protocol-error closure; do not clamp or silently default malformed received fields.

Reason / differences: C++ stores and reads all three progress fields as uint32_t, so negative playback speed is not represented in that path. Its read_uint_field instead logs/drops invalid fields and the containing progress object keeps defaults, unlike this SDK's fail-closed parser. This is evidence for a nonnegative working domain only, not equivalence of error behavior or proof of a normative range. Go intentionally keeps exact values beyond uint32 and floating-point precision boundaries; no C++ integer cap is imported.

Revisit when: An authoritative signed-field/range clarification, a real peer requiring negative/reverse playback, or a deliberate compatibility-policy decision. Existing rejection tests cannot resolve the normative domain.

### WA06 — provisional

Linked obligations: CN15.01, CN15.02, CN24.06, M02.01. Policy evidence: **declared, not executed here**.

Decision: Keep the current bounded pre-Noise capacity refusal and do not import the C++ pre-Noise text-goodbye path. No cleartext application goodbye may be added to bypass the initial encrypted-message sequence.

Reason / differences: C++ releases an excess nursery connection before start_noise_handshake with ANOTHER_SERVER. Its host disconnect invokes send_goodbye_reason, and send_app_json routes to plain text while Noise is inactive. That source path conflicts with our pinned RC1 sequence, so copying it cannot resolve lower-priority refusal semantics. Current cap behavior remains an explicit provisional resource policy, not declared full compliance.

Revisit when: Clarification of the pre-authentication capacity exception versus required encrypted refusal reasons, or an explicitly reviewed admission/resource design. Do not weaken caps or emit early cleartext merely to imitate another implementation.
